terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive; negative dum nē, dummodo nē
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.97: ōderint, dum metuant (Accius, quoted by Cicero; Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 5.4: id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat
terms.comment: The condition on which the main clause holds. The negative is nē, not nōn.

terms.grammar: adverb, with the subjunctive; modo nē, modo ut
terms.comment: “Only let …”: the lighter form; see only.

phrases.english: let them hate, as long as they fear

phrases.latin: opus rūsticum omne cūret utī sciat facere, et id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat
phrases.english: let him make sure he knows how to do every job on the farm, and do it often, as long as he doesn’t tire himself

sources: Lewis & Short: dum · Lewis & Short: dummodo · Lewis & Short: modo
